lines.text: Many learners say: I arrived to the airport at five.
Better: I arrived at the airport at five.
At! We arrived at the hotel.

data.wrong: I arrived to the airport at five.
data.right: I arrived at the airport at five.

native.tip: En español “llegué a”, pero en inglés “arrive” va con “at” (o “in” con ciudades), no con “to.”
native.caption: Muchos dicen “I arrived to the airport at five.” 🙈 En español “llegué a”, pero en inglés “arrive” va con “at” y no con “to”: “I arrived at the airport at five.” ¡Escucha a Carlos y repite! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “at”. Con “arrive” se usa “at” (lugares) o “in” (ciudades), nunca “to”. Escribe una frase tuya con “at”. Practica más con un quiz gratis aquí: {link}

en.tip: In Spanish it is “llegué a”, but English “arrive” takes “at”, not “to.”
en.caption: Many learners say “I arrived to the airport at five.” In Spanish it is “llegué a”, but English “arrive” takes “at” and not “to”: “I arrived at the airport at five.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
